items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1959-07-16
items.q: Yeah I played one parade with Santo.

ctx.x: Well I think I was talking about the mellophone when did you start on that and ever play any parades or anything with that?

Yeah I played one parade with Santo. But the mellophone I come to get the mellophone Bill I was having trouble with the conette players. I'd get to play the jazz you know and the conette players would squawk you see. So I said well I'll have to get something that won't interfere. So I remembered Billy Braun playing mellophone with Brownlee see. But he didn't play he played more straight. He didn't play much jazz on mellophone. items.title: Santo Pecora Interview, 1972-11-09
items.q: Monk Hazel told Hip, he said, man why don't you put a Dixieland band in this?

ctx.x: Meal and Minutes. Meal and Minutes. Yeah.

I was a little bit of a band called Bill Gruber. So they only wanted a four piece band because it was a small stage, smaller than the famous door, see. So they only had four pieces. So I had to leave Sharky go and let the Bouchard go, see. So it was trombone, piano, drums and bass. So when I got finished there, Sharky, Monk Hazel, you know how Sharky got in the famous store? Monk Hazel told Hip, he said, man why don't you put a Dixieland band in this? He said, you're not making money with that Spanish band and…
How many jobs would you work a day with Sharky then?
